card.name: Linking words before a risk statement
card.fires_on: Small words and 'likely' that sit right before a statement of risk or chance, such as 'more likely to develop', 'history of', or 'will be avoided'. The next words usually name a condition or outcome.

modes.label: more likely
modes.description: The word 'likely' after 'more' when saying who is prone to a condition.
modes.example: Patients with a history of genitourinary infections are more<< likely>> to develop genitourinary infections when

modes.label: history of
modes.description: The word 'of' after 'prior history' in a list of risk factors.
modes.example: Patients with a prior history<< of>> peptic ulcer disease and/or GI bleeding

modes.label: will be / it is unknown
modes.description: Linking words in a sentence about whether an outcome will happen.
modes.example: these delays are not a guarantee that neuraxial hematoma will<< be>> avoided.

card.writes: It lowers the odds of words like 'likely' and 'unlikely' coming next, so the model expects a concrete condition or outcome instead.
card.plain: It fires on the small word just before a sentence says what condition or outcome a risk leads to.
